solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ahead, area in the opponent's half of the pitch?

definitions.text: in the opponent's half of the pitch?

parts.note: up, as in 'two goals up', means ahead
a field is an area of ground

explanation.surface: A sports commentator pointing out a zone of the playing field beyond halfway.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by description rather than a dictionary synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing upfield means moving toward or being in the half nearer the goal you attack.

clue.text: Arrangement subject to rank

parts.note: under means subject to, as in 'under orders'
standing is rank or status

explanation.surface: A deal made subject to someone's seniority.
explanation.definitionFit: An understanding is an informal agreement or arrangement between parties.

clue.text: Works with fine performer on tragedy's ending

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
an actor is a performer

indicators.note: a word's ending is its last letter

explanation.surface: A play staged with a good performer in the tragic finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a verb or artistic output, but is the noun for a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Works is a word for an industrial plant, the same as a factory.

clue.text: Guard scratching head in lobby

indicators.note: scratching means striking out, here the head or first letter

parts.note: a sentry is a guard

explanation.surface: A bored security man scratching his head in a hotel foyer.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry or entrance hall is a lobby.

clue.text: Supply food store especially

parts.note: a deli (delicatessen) is a food shop
very means especially or extremely

explanation.surface: Provide a grocery outlet with special goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivery is the act of supplying goods to a customer.

clue.text: In lab of Finnish scientist

indicators.note: the letters sit in the run of words that follows, spanning their boundaries

explanation.surface: A researcher at a laboratory in Finland.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'laB OF FINnish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is informal British slang for a clever researcher or technical expert.

clue.text: Fruit and nuts, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, i.e. nuts

explanation.surface: Fruit and nuts as a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' pretends to be the food but means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The banana is a tropical fruit.

clue.text: Angler, man knocked out when about to steal from British explorer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened word goes round the next piece
knocked out means removed, so this word is taken from the one before

parts.note: an angler is a fisherman
to rob is to steal from

explanation.surface: A fisherman, knocked out, then robbed of something British.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from British' reads as wordplay but 'from' belongs to 'steal from' and 'British' to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Martin Frobisher was an Elizabethan English navigator who sought the Northwest Passage.

clue.text: Second pressing

explanation.definitionFit: Instant means both a very short moment and an urgent need.

clue.text: Actor Alain gripping whip hard in sports event

indicators.note: gripping means holding something within, so the actor's name surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: Alain Delon was a French film actor
a cat (cat-o'-nine-tails) is a whip
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A French film star wielding a whip at an athletics meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The decathlon is a ten-discipline athletics competition.

clue.text: Start working in front of group

indicators.note: places the first piece before the second in the answer

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin operating ahead of a collection of others.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its beginning.

clue.text: Law enforcers, with it, shone by buckling down

indicators.note: buckling means bending out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: blue means sad, i.e. down

explanation.surface: Police officers fastening their shiny belts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buckling' makes THEBOYSIN from IT SHONE BY.
explanation.definitionFit: The boys in blue is an idiom for the police, after their blue uniforms.

clue.text: Heath returned having joined foremost of yachts, very spacious

indicators.note: tells us the next piece is attached after the first
returned means sent back, so the word for heath is read backwards

parts.note: a moor is open heathland

indicators.note: foremost means the very first, so take the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Yachts gathering near open heath with plenty of space for all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heath' suggests former Prime Minister Edward Heath, a famous yachtsman, but it is just open land.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomy describes something with ample space inside.

clue.text: Justify being very mean

parts.note: to indicate is to mean or signify

explanation.surface: Defending oneself for being extremely stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like an adjective (stingy) but is the verb 'signify'.
explanation.definitionFit: To vindicate a claim or action is to show it was right, i.e. justify it.

clue.text: Plays followed by blue film

indicators.note: puts the second piece after the first

parts.note: toys as a verb means plays with idly
blue is the colour of the British Conservative (Tory) party

explanation.surface: Theatre productions followed by a sad movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party, so a 'blue' is a Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Toy Story is the 1995 Pixar animated movie.

clue.text: First-rate crumble and pastry dish served up in restaurant

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate
to rot is to decay or crumble
a tart is a pastry dish

explanation.surface: A top-quality crumble and a tart on an Italian menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses AIROTTART; 'crumble' looks like a pudding but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian restaurant.

clue.text: Hospital within reach in shantytown

indicators.note: within puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: to get to a place is to reach it
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital that can be reached from a poor settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is a deprived, overcrowded urban district, close in sense to a slum or shantytown.

clue.text: Some menial reverentially rising for French poet

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read upwards, i.e. backwards
some of means only a part, so the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A servant bowing respectfully before a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters ENIALREV in 'mENIAL REVerentially' are reversed by 'rising'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Verlaine was a nineteenth-century French Symbolist poet.

clue.text: Delicious drink at hand outside court

indicators.note: outside means around, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: something at hand is near

explanation.surface: A tasty beverage being served just beyond a courtroom or tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is the drink of the gods, used for any delicious beverage.

clue.text: Daily in Canada, originally thinner

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so take the first letter

parts.note: leaner means thinner

explanation.surface: A Canadian newspaper that started out slimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' in Britain is a cleaning woman who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a daily is a domestic help who cleans the house.

clue.text: Accept members carry weapons

parts.note: to bear something is to accept or tolerate it
arms are limbs, i.e. members of the body

explanation.surface: Agree that the club's members may go armed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing arms is the idiom for being armed, as in the US Second Amendment.

clue.text: Witty reply about securing current job

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the first piece encloses the rest

parts.note: re means about or concerning
I is the symbol for electric current
a post is a job

explanation.surface: A sharp comeback about landing a position.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, clever retort.

clue.text: Point the finger at copper in corrupt case

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
corrupt means spoiled or distorted, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Blaming a police officer in a crooked court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal; 'corrupt' rearranges CASE to ACSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To accuse someone is to blame them, idiomatically to point the finger.

clue.text: The very same dialect in broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: The same regional speech is used on a radio or TV programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical things are exactly alike, the very same as each other.

clue.text: Snake by hollowed-out evergreen tree

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: hollowed-out means emptied of its inside, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A serpent lying beside a rotten conifer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evergreen tree' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'tree'.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar known for its trembling leaves.

clue.text: Old prince losing book causes alarm

indicators.note: losing means giving up, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: Albert was Queen Victoria's Prince Consort

explanation.surface: A former prince misplacing a volume creates panic.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is a warning signal, the same as an alarm.

clue.text: One beyond saving in gripping one- reeler

indicators.note: signals that the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A doomed character in a thrilling short silent film.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone or something past help, sure to die or be lost.

clue.text: Building valuers in general

indicators.note: building means constructing, so these letters are assembled into a new form

explanation.surface: Property assessors working on buildings across the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal and general both mean applying to all cases.

clue.text: Sophisticated town close to Nice

parts.note: urban means of a town or city

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so take its final letter

explanation.surface: A chic town near the French Riviera resort of Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the adjective but is the French city.
explanation.definitionFit: An urbane person is polished and suave in manner.

clue.text: Very violent radical

definitions.meaning: ... weather or force is very violent or severe
an ... political view or person is radical

explanation.surface: A politically fanatical person prone to great violence.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme covers both severity of force and holding far-out, radical opinions.
